deviations: Clearance reversal updates only the status field (active->reversed) on the original record, leaving amounts/refs/date/version immutable; balances are derived as sum(active), matching the frozen Clearance entity without a private reverses field.

Clearance has no reason column (reason is audit/receipt only, per the authoritative spec); the cash read returns the effective counterparty from transaction.counterparty_id or the latest unreversed CashPartyMatch.
No canonical clearance.create/reverse channel is exposed; only private services implement them, caller-supplied balances are rejected, and no SourceConsumption/ledger/accounting facts are written.

Some rejection branches (non-active/non-receivable open item, future cash date) are unreachable through existing DB constraints/posting rules; services still guard them and tests cover all constructible paths.

create_clearance takes a versioned cash_transaction_ref ({namespace,kind,id,version}) instead of the bare cash_transaction_id in the spec signature, so a stale cash version is rejected before the company lock; the model still persists cash_transaction_id plus the ref JSON.

PM read scope: open_item_balances/clearance_list/aging stay readable for a PM's managed project, but cash_candidates_for_open_item returns [] for PM because the cash named read interface is owner/finance/auditor-only per the spec's cash restriction; the page renders balances/history with the read-only notice instead of returning 403 (Lead-adjudicated interpretation).

verify_integrity treats the cleared event as append-only: every clearance (active or reversed) must have exactly one settlement.cleared.v1 event, and a reversed clearance must additionally have exactly one settlement.clearance_reversed.v1 event; the earlier 'reversed must not have a cleared event' rule would have forced deleting an append-only event.
